forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: West Yorkshire Mayor's budget letter cites a recurring police funding gap, without giving an amount
news_drafts.lead:
A budget submission from the West Yorkshire Combined Authority, a body run by several councils together with a mayor, says West Yorkshire Police faces a recurring funding gap from year to year. The submission is a letter in the papers for the authority's board meeting on 29 October 2026, and it says the Mayor wants the gap addressed. The letter gives no amount for it.

The letter describes the force's financial management as strong. It says the gap remains "despite strong financial management and the continued application of a rigorous Priority Based Budgeting approach". That is the letter's wording about the force's budgeting method.

The letter says this pressure affects the force's ability to sustain current policing levels. It sets out no figures for the gap or for the policing that might be affected.
news_drafts.paper_title: Item 13 - Appendix 1 - West Yorkshire Combined Authority Budget Submission

news_drafts.headline: West Yorkshire Combined Authority and Police fund part of their borrowing need from own cash, not loans
news_drafts.lead:
West Yorkshire Combined Authority, the body run by the region's councils for transport and economic growth, and West Yorkshire Police are both paying for part of their long-term spending from their own cash rather than from loans. The first-quarter treasury management update (how a body borrows, invests spare cash and manages the risks of both) goes to the Governance & Audit Committee on 8 October 2026.

The update says both continue to hold an "under-borrowed" position. Each has a capital financing requirement (CFR), the total spent on long-lived assets that has not yet been paid for, in effect its underlying need to borrow. A proportion of that is being met from cash balances and reserves, money set aside, rather than external borrowing. This is known as internal borrowing, which saves interest but uses up the cushion.

The paper says the approach reduces borrowing costs in the short term and "remains appropriate while cash balances are strong and PWLB borrowing rates remain comparatively high". The PWLB, the Public Works Loan Board, is the government's lending arm for councils and where most council borrowing comes from. The paper gives no figure for the share funded from cash.

findings.paper_title: Item 14 - Integrated Business, Budget & Workforce Planning Approach 2027-28
findings.headline: The 2027/28 budget timetable sets final approval for January/February 2027, after a December 2026 Board update on the Autumn Budget implications.
findings.detail: The paper says a further report in December 2026 will set out the potential implications of the Autumn Budget, key principles and assumptions, and a draft Mayoral budget. Final sign-off is scheduled for the January/February 2027 Board.
findings.matters: The timing of the Autumn Budget against the statutory budget deadline is a constraint other councils setting 2027/28 budgets will face too.
findings.quote: Approve the final budget and business plan in line with statutory deadlines.

findings.paper_title: Item 14 - Integrated Business, Budget & Workforce Planning Approach 2027-28
findings.headline: The paper states the Authority 'has built up a modest level of reserves' and has a 'strong track record of managing within its financial envelope'.
findings.detail: The paper presents these points alongside the financial risks, and says fiscal devolution provides an opportunity to mitigate them. The paper does not give a reserves figure.
findings.matters: A finance director comparing reserve positions across councils would want the balance behind the description, which this paper does not provide.
findings.quote: the Authority has a strong track record of managing within its financial envelope and has built up a modest level of reserves

findings.paper_title: Item 14 - Integrated Business, Budget & Workforce Planning Approach 2027-28
findings.headline: The paper describes the Authority's funding model as having 'inconsistency and short-term income streams with very low levels of capacity funding'.
findings.detail: The paper names long-term financial sustainability and resilience against short-term fiscal shocks as its most significant financial risks. It links this risk to the bus franchising transfer.
findings.matters: Short-term income streams and low capacity funding are a risk that other combined authorities and lenders assessing similar models will also weigh.
findings.quote: a funding model that has been characterised by inconsistency and short-term income streams with very low levels of capacity funding

findings.paper_title: Item 14 - Integrated Business, Budget & Workforce Planning Approach 2027-28
findings.headline: The Authority reports that it will take on the risk and reward of the bus network through franchising, with a new financial model taking effect from May 2027.
findings.detail: The paper says cost and income estimates for the new financial model are being refined. It notes that existing operational transport financial pressures will continue to be managed until the Authority has full control of the public bus network.
findings.matters: Taking on the risk and reward of a bus network shifts cost and income exposure to the authority, which bears on budget resilience for transport authorities planning franchising.
findings.quote: refining cost and income estimates for the new financial model that will take effect from May 2027

findings.paper_title: Item 14 - Integrated Business, Budget & Workforce Planning Approach 2027-28
findings.headline: The Authority reports that the Rewiring the State Cabinet Statement announces a share of business rates income for Mayoral Strategic Authorities from April 2027, with details not yet known.
findings.detail: The paper says the announcement has significant implications for the Authority's future financial model. It states that the details of how the share will work are not known yet, and that further detail is expected in the Autumn Budget statement and the Fiscal Devolution Roadmap.
findings.matters: A new business rates share from April 2027 would change the funding base of a Mayoral Strategic Authority, and other councils and lenders will want to see how the detail is set out.
findings.quote: the announcement to give Mayoral Strategic Authorities a share of business rates income from April 2027
